artworks.title: Acrisius Orders Danaë and Perseus into the Chest
artworks.description: Attic red-figure of Acrisius casting Danaë and Perseus to sea — Abas' grandson in the Argive stemma, the dynasty that begins when Lynceus' son divides the kingdom between twin heirs.

artworks.title: Melampus healing the daughters of Proetus
artworks.description: Lucanian nestoris: Melampus cures the Proetides — Abas' other grandson Proetus' house, the twin line that fought Acrisius even in the womb.

popCulture.title: Abas (son of Lynceus)
popCulture.description: Early king of Argos, son of Lynceus and Hypermnestra — father of the warring twins Acrisius and Proetus. Not the centaur Abas nor other catalogue namesakes.

popCulture.title: Acrisius
popCulture.description: Abas' son who rules Argos and locks Danaë away — the Perseid grandfather line descends through this twin.

popCulture.title: Proetus
popCulture.description: Abas' other son — the twin who takes Tiryns, host of Bellerophon and father of the Proetides.

popCulture.title: Lynceus of Argos
popCulture.description: Abas' father — the sole son of Aegyptus spared by Hypermnestra on the Danaids' wedding night.
